mainText:
Good morning, it's Saturday, Aug. 29.

Nepal flood death toll nears 600 as rescue efforts continue.
More than 3,700 people have been rescued as crews search for survivors following Wednesday's massive flood along the Nepal-China border. At least 579 people have been killed in Nepal and five in Tibet, while roughly 2,500 remain missing; authorities are monitoring
newly formed lakes
upstream for risks of further flooding. See how the glacier collapse triggered the flood.
Iran war reaches six-month mark.
Six months after fighting began between Iran, Israel, and the US, diplomatic efforts have yet to produce an agreement to end the conflict. At least 18 US service members have been killed and more than 750 wounded, while the Pentagon estimates the war has cost the US more than $37.5B. How the world has changed since the war began. ... and how the war affects you.
Norway's King Harald V dies at 89 after 35 years on the throne.
Harald died yesterday after being hospitalized with a rare blood disorder and later developing a bacterial bloodstream infection. The monarch, who took the throne in 1991, is succeeded by his 53-year-old son, Haakon; Haakon's 22-year-old daughter, Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra, is now heir to the throne. Which countries still have monarchies?
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh signals interest rate hikes may be needed.
Warsh yesterday said the Federal Reserve has "work to do" if underlying inflation does not move toward the central bank's 2% target quickly enough. The comments, delivered during his first Jackson Hole speech as Fed chair, led investors to increase their expectations for a September rate hike. Read Warsh's speech. How raising interest rates controls inflation.
Dolly Parton's music streams surge more than 2,000% after her death.
US audio and video streams of Parton's catalog jumped from 1.2 million Monday to 30.5 million Tuesday, the day the country music icon died at age 80. "Jolene" led the surge, climbing from roughly 196,000 streams to 3.3 million, while "9 to 5" jumped to 3 million. "Islands in the Stream" and "I Will Always Love You" each topped 2 million. Explore resources 1440 staff has collected about Parton.
Thousands rally for voting rights in Washington, DC.
Demonstrators gathered on the National Mall yesterday for the Defend the Vote march, held 63 years after Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I Have a Dream" speech at the 1963 March on Washington. The rally comes amid changes to voting rules and
congressional maps
ahead of November's midterm elections. See photos from the march.
